slide.title: Make AI Sound Like You
slide.body: Two speech bubbles: left grey, filled with faint generic lines; right teal, with a coffee cup icon and a small page labelled 'Voice guide' clipped to it. Small tag: AI for Content Creators · Lesson 2.

scenes.voiceover: Ask an AI assistant to write a post about your new coffee, and you get something like this. Discover the rich, bold flavour of our new blend. It is not wrong. It just sounds like everyone. And your brand is not everyone.

slide.title: Teaching AI Your Brand Voice
slide.body: AI for Content Creators and Marketers · Lesson 2 of 15

scenes.voiceover: In the last lesson, we mapped where AI fits in your workflow. Now we make it sound like your brand. A chat assistant has read a huge amount of text. So without guidance, it writes in a safe, average style, the most common kind of marketing language.

slide.title: A one-page voice guide
slide.body: A single page divided into four labelled boxes: Personality · Words to use · Words to avoid · Example posts.

scenes.voiceover: To get text that sounds like you, give the assistant your brand voice as context. You do this with a brand voice guide. It is a short document, and one page is enough. It has four parts.

slide.title: Parts 1 to 3
slide.body: Personality: 3–5 adjectives with explanations ('warm, not childish'; 'expert, not formal') · Words to use: product names, greetings · Words to avoid: overused marketing words, claims you cannot prove

scenes.voiceover: First, personality. Choose three to five adjectives, each with a short explanation, such as warm, not childish, or expert, not formal. Second, words to use, like the way you name your products or greet customers. Third, words to avoid, such as overused marketing words or claims you cannot prove.

slide.title: Part 4: Example posts
slide.body: Large quote: "Examples teach style better than descriptions." Below: two small post cards with a green tick.

scenes.voiceover: Fourth, example posts. Add two or three real posts that sound exactly right. Examples teach style better than any description.

slide.title: How to use the guide
slide.body:
[Voice guide pasted here]

Using the voice guide above, write a caption for…

Side note with a lock icon: No confidential plans, customer data or contracts.

scenes.voiceover: Paste the guide at the start of a conversation, or save it in the tool's project or custom instructions feature, if your plan has one. Then add your request after it. And only include information you are allowed to share. Never paste confidential plans or customer data into an AI tool.

scenes.stock_query: new employee welcomed by team office
scenes.on_screen_text: Notes for a new team member
scenes.voiceover: Think of the voice guide as the notes you give a new team member on their first day. A talented writer still needs to know how your company speaks to customers. Without those notes, they write in their own general style. With them, their work starts to sound like the team.
Let's see it work. Valentina manages marketing for a sample coffee brand from a family farm in the hills near Medellín, in Colombia. The brand sells whole beans online.

slide.title: Without the guide
slide.body: Grey post card: "Elevate your mornings with our exquisite new blend! Rich, smooth and bursting with flavour. Order now and taste the difference! #coffee #coffeelover"

scenes.voiceover: First, she asks for an Instagram caption for a new washed coffee, with no guide. The answer says: elevate your mornings with our exquisite new blend, rich, smooth and bursting with flavour. It could be any coffee brand in the world.

slide.title: Valentina's voice guide
slide.body: Personality: warm like a family table; proud without boasting; clear about how coffee is made. Use: 'our farm', 'the harvest', 'the Suárez family'. Avoid: 'elevate', 'exquisite', 'bursting with flavour', health claims. Examples: 2 liked captions.

scenes.voiceover: Then she writes a short guide. Personality: warm like a family table, proud of the farm without boasting. Use: our farm, the harvest, the Suárez family. Avoid: elevate, exquisite, bursting with flavour, and health claims. She adds two past captions that followers liked.

slide.title: With the guide
slide.body: Teal post card: "This harvest, Don Álvaro tried something new: washing the beans before drying them. The result is a cleaner cup with notes of red apple and brown sugar. Small batch, from our farm to your kitchen."

scenes.voiceover: She pastes the guide and repeats the request. The new caption says: this harvest, Don Álvaro tried something new, washing the beans before drying them. The result is a cleaner cup with notes of red apple and brown sugar. Small batch, from our farm to your kitchen.

slide.title: Three differences, one check
slide.body: 1. Names a person · 2. Plain tasting notes · 3. No empty words. Amber flag on 'red apple': invented, check with the farm.

scenes.voiceover: She lists three differences. The second caption names a person, uses plain tasting notes and removes the empty words. But she still checks it. The AI invented red apple from general coffee knowledge, so she confirms the tasting notes with the farm. She also changes one phrase to match how Don Álvaro describes the process himself.

A common mistake is a guide that is only adjectives, like friendly, professional and fun. Almost every brand could use those words. Add clear use and avoid lists and, most important, real example posts. The second mistake is trusting the improved text completely. A better style does not mean correct facts.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. No context = average style. 2. Voice guide: personality, use, avoid, examples. 3. Sounds right ≠ correct: review facts and voice.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, without context, AI writes in an average style that could belong to any brand. Second, a one-page voice guide with personality, words to use, words to avoid and example posts helps AI match your brand. Third, text that sounds right can still contain invented details, so always review it for facts and voice.

Now it is your turn. In the exercise below, write a one-page voice guide for a real or sample brand. Then ask Claude or ChatGPT for the same post, once without the guide and once with it, and list three differences. It takes about twenty minutes. In the next lesson, Audience Research and Personas with AI, we learn who we are writing for. See you there.
